shlokas.text: शशिरा शयष्ठ चक्र तेऽशकलायोजनानि यवजगणाः । प्राणेनैति कलां भःखयुगांशे ग्रहजवो भवांशेऽर्कः
shlokas.english_draft: The revolutions of the Sun, Moon, and planets, their degrees and minutes, and the distances in yojanas are represented through the alphabetical system. The sphere of the asterisms turns through one minute of arc in one prana (respiration). The speed of a planet is one yojana per 1/60 of a prana (or cosmic time division).

shlokas.text: शनिगुरुकज खकगाधं भगबंध ख सूचाङ्गलो घहस्तोना
shlokas.english_draft: The diameters of the orbits or globes of Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, Mercury, the Sun, and the Moon are given in yojanas, measured in terms of fingers (angulas) and cubits (hastas) according to the Gitika reckoning.

shlokas.text: मन्दात् ङ ख द ज डा वक्रिणां द्वितीये पर जाणलछल कनोच्चाच्छीघ्रात गियिङश कुवायुकक्ष्यान्त्या
shlokas.english_draft: The degrees of the epicycles of mandocca (apogee) and shighrocca (fast apex/conjunction) for the planets (Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, Mercury) at the end of the first and third quadrants, and for retrogression (vakra), as well as the height of the atmosphere surrounding the Earth (ku-vayu-kaksya).

shlokas.text: भपञ्जरे ज्ञात्वा । ग्रहभगणपरिभ्रमणं स याति भित्त्वा परं ब्रह्म
shlokas.english_draft: Whoever knows this movement of the planets and asterisms in the sphere of the starry firmament (bha-panjara) pierces through the spheres and attains the Supreme Brahman.

shlokas.text: एक दश च शतञ्च सहस्रमयुतनियुते तथा प्रयुतम् । कोट्यर्बुदञ्च वृन्दं स्थानात्स्थानं दशगुणं स्यात्
shlokas.english_draft: Eka (one), dasha (ten), shata (hundred), sahasra (thousand), ayuta (ten thousand), niyuta (hundred thousand), prayuta (million), koti (ten million), arbuda (hundred million), and vrinda (billion); each place is ten times the preceding place.

shlokas.text: भाग हरेदवर्गान्नित्यं द्विगुणेन वर्गमूलेन ।वर्गाद्वगै शुद्ध लब्धं स्थानान्तरे मूलम्
shlokas.english_draft: Always divide the non-square digit by twice the square root (already extracted). Subtracting the square of the quotient digit from the square place, the quotient placed in the next position gives the root digit.

shlokas.text: अघनाट्नजे द्वितीयात् त्रिगुणेन घनस्य मूलवर्गण ।वर्गस्त्रिपूर्वगुणितश्शोध्यः प्रथमादघनश्च घनाद
shlokas.english_draft: Dividing the non-cube place by thrice the square of the cube root, subtract the square of the quotient multiplied by thrice the previous root digit from the next non-cube place, and subtract the cube of the quotient digit from the cube place.

shlokas.text: त्रिभुज क्षेत्र ,, का फल होगर ।' एवं आधीगीतिका अर्थ हुभा ॥जव भजातत्संवर्गाधं स घनष्पडनिरिति
shlokas.english_draft: The area of a triangle is half the product of the base and the height (perpendicular). The volume of a solid having six edges (pyramid/tetrahedron) is one-sixth of the product of the base area and height.

shlokas.text: चतुरधिकं शतमष्टगुणं द्वाषष्टिस्तथा सहस्राणाम् । अयुत्नद्वयविष्कम्भस्यासन्नो वृत्तपरिणाहः
shlokas.english_draft: Add 4 to 100, multiply by 8, and add 62,000; this gives 62,832. This is the approximate circumference of a circle whose diameter is 20,000 (yielding π ≈ 3.1416).

shlokas.text: प्रथमाच्चापज्यार्धाद्यरूनं खण्डितं द्वितीया। तत्पथमज्याधीशस्तैस्तैरूनानि शेषाणि
shlokas.english_draft: Subtracting from the first half-chord (sine segment) its fraction, and dividing by the first sine-difference, the successive sine-differences (R-sine segments) are obtained.

shlokas.text: वृत्तं भ्रमेण साध्यं त्रिभुजञ्च चतुर्भुजञ्च कर्णाभ्याम् ॥ साध्या जलेन समभूरधऊवं लम्बकेनैव
shlokas.english_draft: A circle is drawn with a compass; triangles and quadrilaterals are constructed by means of their diagonals. Level ground is tested with water, and verticality is determined with a plumb-line.

shlokas.text: शोः प्रमाणवर्ग छायावर्गण संयुतं कृत्वा । यत्तस्य वर्गमूलं विष्कम्भाधं स्ववसस्य
shlokas.english_draft: Adding the square of the gnomon's height to the square of its shadow, the square root of the sum is the hypotenuse of the gnomon shadow triangle (the radius of the shadow circle).

shlokas.text: गीतिकापादः॥ शङ्कुगुणं शंङ कुभुजाविवरं शङ्कुभुजयोर्विशेषहृतम् यल्लब्धं सा छाया ज्ञेया शङ्कोस्स्वमूलाद्धि
shlokas.english_draft: Multiply the height of the gnomon by the distance between the two gnomons, and divide by the difference between the two gnomons' heights (or shadow differences); the quotient obtained is the length of the shadow measured from the base of the gnomon.

shlokas.text: छायागुणितं छायाग्रविवरमनेन भाजिता कोटी। शङ्कगुणा कोटी सा छायाभक्ता भुजा भवति
shlokas.english_draft: The shadow multiplied by the distance between the tips of the shadows and divided by the difference gives the upright (koti); the upright multiplied by the gnomon height and divided by the shadow gives the base (bhuja).

shlokas.text: गीतिकापादः ॥ ग्रासोने द्वे वृत्ते ग्रासगुणे भाजयेत्पृथतत्त्वेन । ग्रासोनयोगभक्ते संपातशरौ परस्परतः
shlokas.english_draft: For two intersecting circles, multiply the diameter of each circle diminished by the eclipse (overlap/grasa) separately by the eclipse, and divide by the sum of the diameters diminished by the eclipse; the resulting quotients are the arrows (arrows of intersection/sampata-shara) of the respective circles.

shlokas.text: समवृत्तपरिधिपादं छिन्द्यात्रिभुजाचर्भुजाच्चैव। समाचापज्यानि तु विष्कम्भाध यथेष्टानि
shlokas.english_draft: Divide the quadrant of a circle into desired equal arcs using triangles and quadrilaterals; the half-chords (sines) corresponding to these equal arcs are determined relative to the radius.

shlokas.text: गीतिकापादः ॥ गच्छोऽष्टोत्तरगुणिताद्विगुणाद्युत्तरविशेषवर्गयुतात् ।मूलं द्विगुणाधूनं स्वोत्तरभजितं सरूपा
shlokas.english_draft: To find the number of terms (gaccha) in an arithmetic progression: multiply the sum by 8 times the common difference, add the square of (twice the first term minus the common difference), take the square root, subtract twice the first term, divide by the common difference, and add 1, then divide by 2.

shlokas.text: एकोत्तराद्यपचितेर्गच्छाद्यकोत्तरत्रिसंवर्गः । षड्भक्तस्स चितिघनस्सैकपदघनो विमूलो वा
shlokas.english_draft: The product of three consecutive integers starting from the number of terms plus one, divided by 6, is the sum of triangular numbers (chiti-ghana, or sum of sums of natural numbers: n(n+1)(n+2)/6).

shlokas.text: ।संपर्कस्य हि वर्गाद्विशोधयेदेव वर्गसंपर्कम् । यत्तस्य भवत्यधं विद्यादगुणकारसंवर्गम्
shlokas.english_draft: Subtract the sum of squares of two quantities from the square of their sum; half of the remainder is known as the product of those two quantities.

shlokas.text: द्विकृतिगुणात्संवर्गाद द्वयन्तरवर्गण संयुतान्मूलम् ।अन्तरयुक्तं हीनं तद्गुणकारद्वयं दलितम्
shlokas.english_draft: Multiply four times the product of two quantities by the square of their difference, take the square root; adding and subtracting the difference and halving the results gives the two original quantities separately.

shlokas.text: मूलफलं सफलं कालमूलगुणमर्धमूलकृतियुक्तम् । मूलं मूलार्धोनं कालहृतं स्यात्स्वमूलफलम्
shlokas.english_draft: To find the principal interest rate: multiply the total interest plus principal by the time period and principal factor, add the square of half the principal, take the square root, subtract half the principal, and divide by time; this yields the interest on the principal.

shlokas.text: त्रैराशिकालराशिं तमथेच्छाराशिना हतं कृत्वा । लब्धप्रमाणभजितं तस्मादिच्छाफलमिदं स्यात्
shlokas.english_draft: In the Rule of Three: multiply the requisition quantity (iccha-rashi) by the fruit quantity (phala-rashi), and divide by the measure quantity (pramana-rashi); the result obtained is the desired fruit (iccha-phala).

shlokas.text: गुणकारा भागहरा भागेहरा ये भवन्ति गुणकाराः ।यः क्षेपस्सो ऽपचयो ऽपचयः क्षेपश्च विपरीते
shlokas.english_draft: In the inverse method (Viparita-ganita): multipliers become divisors and divisors become multipliers; additions become subtractions and subtractions become additions.

shlokas.text: २९ ॥गुलिकान्तरेण विभजेवयोः पुरुषयोस्तु रूपकविशेषम् । लब्धं गुलिका मूल्यं यद्यर्थकृतं भवति तुल्यम्
shlokas.english_draft: Divide the difference in known amounts (rupaka) owned by two persons by the difference in the number of unknown items (gulika) they possess; the quotient is the price of one unknown item, provided their total wealth is equal.

shlokas.text: अधिकाग्रभागहारं छिन्द्यादूनाग्रभागहारेण । शेषपरस्परभक्त मतिगुणमग्रान्तरें क्षिप्तम्
shlokas.english_draft: In the pulverized method (Kuttaka for indeterminate equations): divide the divisor yielding the greater remainder by the divisor yielding the lesser remainder, continue mutual division of remainders, choose an assumed multiplier (mati) such that when multiplied by the last remainder and added to the difference of remainders...

shlokas.text: अधउपरिगुणितमन्त्ययुगूनाग्रच्छेदभाजिते शेषम् । अधिकाग्रच्छेदगुणं द्विच्छेदाग्रमधिकाग्रयुतम्
shlokas.english_draft: ...multiply from bottom to top, adding the next term, divide by the lesser remainder's divisor; the final remainder multiplied by the greater remainder's divisor and added to the greater remainder gives the solution for two divisors.

shlokas.text: भताराग्रहविधरं व्यासाहितस्स्वकर्णसंवर्गः। कक्ष्यायां ग्रहवेगो यो भवति स मन्दनीचोच्चे
shlokas.english_draft: The distance between stars and planets, the product of their radii and hypotenuse, and the velocity of a planet in its orbit at mandocca (apogee) and mandanica (perigee).

shlokas.text: रव्यब्दा रविशशियोगा भवन्ति शशिमासाः। रविभूयोगा दिवसा भावर्ताश्वापि नाक्षत्राः
shlokas.english_draft: Solar years are determined by the Sun's revolutions; lunar months by the conjunctions of the Sun and Moon; civil days (savana days) by the solar-terrestrial revolutions; and sidereal days by the rotations of the celestial sphere.

shlokas.text: अधिमासका युगे ते रविमासेभ्यो ऽधिकास्तु ये चान्द्राः। शशिदिवसा विज्ञेया भूदिवसोनास्तिथिप्रलयाः
shlokas.english_draft: Intercalary lunar months (adhimasa) in a yuga are the excess of lunar months over solar months; omitted lunar days (tithi-ksaya) are the excess of lunar days over civil (earth) days.

shlokas.text: रविवर्ष मानुष्यं तदपि त्रिंशद्गुणं भवति पित्र्यम् । पित्र्यं द्वादशगुणितं दिव्यं वर्ष समुद्विष्टम्
shlokas.english_draft: A human year is one solar year; thirty human years make one month of the ancestors (Pitris); twelve ancestor months (360 human years) make one divine year (divya-varsa) of the gods.

shlokas.text: पष्ट्यब्दानां षष्टिर्यदा व्यतीतास्त्रयश्च युगपादाः। त्र्यधिका विंशतिरब्दास्तदेह मम जन्मनो ऽतीताः
shlokas.english_draft: When sixty times sixty years (3600 years) and three quarters of the Yuga (Kali Yuga onset) had elapsed, twenty-three years had passed since my birth (Aryabhata was 23 years old at 3600 Kali Yuga, corresponding to 499 CE).

shlokas.text: युगवर्षमासदिवसास्समं प्रवृत्तास्तु चैत्रशुक्लादेः । कालो ऽयमनाद्यन्तो ग्रहभैरनुमीयते क्षेत्रे
shlokas.english_draft: Yugas, years, months, and days began simultaneously at the beginning of the bright fortnight of Chaitra; time is without beginning or end, measured by the movements of planets and stars in space.

shlokas.text: षष्द्या सूर्याब्दानां प्रपूरयन्ति ग्रहा भपरिणाहम् । दिव्येन नभःपरिधिं समं भ्रमन्तस्स्वकक्ष्यासु
shlokas.english_draft: All planets, moving equally at their own speeds in their respective orbits, complete a distance equal to the circumference of the firmament in a divine period.

shlokas.text: मण्डलमल्पमधस्तात् कालेनाल्पेन पूरयति चन्द्रः । उपरिष्ठात्सर्वेषां महच्च महता शनैश्वारी
shlokas.english_draft: The Moon, moving in a smaller lower orbit, completes its circuit in a short time; Saturn, moving in the highest and largest orbit, completes its circuit in a long time.

shlokas.text: अल्पे हि मण्लेऽल्पा महति महान्तश्च राशयो ज्ञेयाः । अंशाः कलास्तथैवं विभागतुल्यावकक्ष्यासु
shlokas.english_draft: In a small orbit the signs (rashis) are small; in a large orbit they are large. Yet the divisions of degrees (amsha) and minutes (kala) are proportionally equal in all orbits.

shlokas.text: भानामधश्शनैश्चरसुरगुरुभौमार्कशुक्रबुधचन्द्राः। तेषामधश्च भूमिमधीभूता खमध्यस्था
shlokas.english_draft: Below the fixed stars lie Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon; below all of them lies the Earth, situated in the center of space.

shlokas.text: सप्तते होरेशाश्शनैश्चराद्या यथाक्रमं शीघ्राः। शीघ्रक्रमाच्चतुर्था भवन्ति सूर्योदयादिनपाः
shlokas.english_draft: The lords of the hours (hora) are the seven planets in decreasing order of orbital period starting from Saturn. The lord of each day starts at sunrise and is the fourth planet in order of speed.

shlokas.text: कक्ष्याप्रतिमण्डलगा भ्रमन्ति सर्व ग्रहास्स्वचारेण । मन्दोच्चादनुलोमं प्रतिलोमञ्चैव शीघ्रोच्चात्
shlokas.english_draft: All planets move in their own orbits and eccentric circles (pratimandala); direct (anuloma) motion is relative to mandocca (apogee) and retrograde/inverse (pratiloma) relative to shighrocca.

shlokas.text: कक्ष्यामण्डलतुल्यंस्वं-स्वं प्रतिमण्डलं भवत्येषाम् । प्रतिमण्डलस्य मध्यं घनभूमध्यादतिक्रान्तम्
shlokas.english_draft: Each planet's eccentric circle is equal in size to its mean orbit, but the center of the eccentric circle is displaced from the center of the solid Earth.

shlokas.text: अनुलोमगानि मन्दाच्छीघ्रात्प्रतिलोमगानि वृत्तानि। कक्ष्यामण्डललनस्ववृत्तमध्ये ग्रहो मध्यः
shlokas.english_draft: The motion in epicycles is direct with respect to mandocca and retrograde with respect to shighrocca; the mean planet lies at the center of its epicycle attached to the deferent orbit.

shlokas.text: मन्दोच्चाच्छीघ्रोच्चादर्धमृणधनं ग्रहेषु मन्देषु। मन्दोच्चातस्फुटमध्याश्शीघ्रोच्चाच्च स्फुटा ज्ञेयाः
shlokas.english_draft: Half the correction for mandocca and shighrocca is applied negatively or positively to the mean position; applying mandocca yields true-mean, and applying shighrocca yields the true position of planets.

shlokas.text: २३ ॥शीघ्रोच्चादोंन कर्तव्यमृणंधनंस्वमन्दोच्चे। स्फुटमध्यौ तु भृगुबुधौ सिद्धान्मन्दात्स्फुटौ भवतः
shlokas.english_draft: The correction from shighrocca is subtracted or added relative to mandocca; for Venus and Mercury, true-mean positions are derived from mandocca, and true positions from shighrocca.

shlokas.text: आर्यभटीयेअथ गोलपाद आरभ्यते । तत्रापमण्डलसंस्थानमाह । मेषादेः कन्यान्तं सममुदगपमण्डलार्धमपयातम् ।तौल्यादेर्मीनान्तं शेषाधैं दक्षिणेनैव
shlokas.english_draft: Here begins Golapada. Half of the ecliptic from the beginning of Aries to the end of Virgo lies to the north of the equator; the remaining half from Libra to Pisces lies to the south.

shlokas.text: ताराग्रहेन्दुपाता भ्रमन्त्यजखमपमण्डलेऽर्कश्च । अकीच मण्डलार्धे भ्रमति हि तस्मिन् क्षितिच्छाया
shlokas.english_draft: The Sun, Moon, star-planets, and lunar nodes move continuously along the ecliptic; opposite the Sun by half a circle moves the Earth's shadow.

shlokas.text: अपमण्डलस्य चन्द्रः पाताद्यात्युत्तरेण दक्षिणतः। गुरुकुजकोणाश्चैवं शीघ्रोच्वेनापि बुधशुक्रौ
shlokas.english_draft: From its node, the Moon moves north or south of the ecliptic; Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, Mercury, and Venus similarly deviate in latitude according to their nodes and shighrocca.

shlokas.text: चन्द्रोंऽशैादशभिरविक्षिप्तोऽर्कान्तरस्थितैश्यः । नवभिभृगुर्भूगोस्तैवर्य धिकैद्वर्यधिकैर्यथालक्षणाः
shlokas.english_draft: The Moon is visible when separated from the Sun by 12 degrees; Venus by 9 degrees; and the other planets (Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, Mercury) by increments of 2 degrees as specified.

shlokas.text: भग्रहभानां गोलार्धानि स्वच्छायया विवर्णानि ।अर्धानि यथासारं सूर्याभिमुखानि दीप्यन्ते
shlokas.english_draft: One half of the globes of the planets and stars is darkened by their own shadow; the other half facing the Sun is illuminated according to their nature.

shlokas.text: अनुलोमगतिौस्थः पश्यत्यचलं विलोमगं यद्वत् । अचलानि भानि तद्वत् समपश्चिमगानि लडायाम्
shlokas.english_draft: Just as a person in a boat moving forward sees stationary objects moving backward, so to an observer at Lanka the fixed stars appear to move uniformly westward.

shlokas.text: यद्वत् कदम्बपुष्पग्रन्थिः प्रचितस्समन्ततः कुसुमैः । तद्वद्धि सर्वसत्त्वैर्जलजैस्स्थजश्व भूगोलः
shlokas.english_draft: Just as a Kadamba flower ball is covered on all sides with blossoms, so the terrestrial globe is covered on all sides with living creatures, both aquatic and terrestrial.

shlokas.text: ब्रम्हदिवसेन भूमेरुपरिष्टाद्योजनं भवति वृद्धिः। दिनतुल्ययैव रात्र्या मुंदपचितायास्तदिह हानिः
shlokas.english_draft: During a day of Brahma, the Earth expands upward by one yojana; during a night of Brahma, equal in duration to the day, it contracts by the same amount.

shlokas.text: उदयास्तमयनिमित्तं नित्यं प्रवहेण वायुनाक्षिप्तः। लंकासमपश्चिमगो भपञ्जरस्सग्रहो भ्रमति
shlokas.english_draft: Impelled by the Pravaha wind, the stellar sphere along with the planets rotates constantly westward relative to Lanka, causing daily rising and setting.

shlokas.text: उदयो योलङ्कायां सो ऽस्तमयस्सवितुरेव सिद्धपुरे।मध्यान्हो यवकोट्यां रोमकविषये ऽर्धरात्रस्स्यात्
shlokas.english_draft: When it is sunrise at Lanka, it is sunset at Siddhapura, noon at Yavakoti, and midnight in the land of Romaka.

shlokas.text: स्थलजलमध्याल्ला भूकक्ष्याया भवेच्चतुर्भागे।उज्जयिनी लङ्कायास्तच्चतुरंशे समोचरतः
shlokas.english_draft: Ujjain is situated one-fourth of the Earth's circumference due north of Lanka, at the boundary between land and water.

shlokas.text: भूव्यासाधनोनं दृश्यं देशात्समाद्गोलार्धम् । अधं भूमिच्छन्नम् भूव्यासार्धाधिकञ्चैव
shlokas.english_draft: From a level surface on Earth, slightly less than half of the celestial sphere is visible (diminished by the Earth's radius); the remaining half is hidden by the Earth.

shlokas.text: देवाः पश्यन्ति भगोलार्धमुदङमेरुसंस्थितास्तव्यम् ।अपसव्यगं तथा दक्षिणघडवामुखे प्रेताः
shlokas.english_draft: The gods situated at the North Pole (Meru) see the northern half of the celestial sphere rotating clockwise; the spirits at the South Pole (Vadavamukha) see it rotating counterclockwise.

shlokas.text: पूर्वापरमधऊधु मण्डलमथ दक्षिणोत्तरजव। क्षितिजं समपार्श्वस्थं भानां यत्रोदयास्तमयौ
shlokas.english_draft: The prime vertical (east-west), meridian (north-south), and horizon (khitija) intersect; the horizon is the circle where stars rise and set.

shlokas.text: मेरुयोजनमात्रः प्रभाकरो हिमवता परिक्षिप्तः। नन्दनवनस्य मध्ये रत्नमयस्सर्वतोवृत्तः
shlokas.english_draft: Mount Meru is one yojana in height, surrounded by the Himalayas, located in the midst of the Nandanavana garden, gem-like and round on all sides.

shlokas.text: पूर्वापरदिओखाधवोर्खा दक्षिणोत्तरस्था च। एतासां संपातो द्रष्टा यस्मिन् भवेद्देशै
shlokas.english_draft: The point of intersection of the east-west vertical circle, zenith-nadir circle, and north-south circle is the place where the observer is situated.

shlokas.text: काष्ठमयं समवृत्तं समन्ततस्समगुरुं लधु गोलम्। पारततैलजलस्तं भ्रमयेत्वधिया च कालसमम्
shlokas.english_draft: Construct a sphere of wood, perfectly circular and uniform in weight; rotate it continuously at a uniform rate matching time using mercury, oil, and water through human intellect.

shlokas.text: दुग्गोलार्धकपाले ज्याधैन विकल्पयेङगोलार्धम्। विषुवज्जीवाक्षभुजा तस्यास्त्ववलम्बकः कोटिः
shlokas.english_draft: In the hemisphere of the armillary sphere, half-chords represent the celestial positions; the sine of latitude is the base (bhuja), and the sine of co-latitude is the upright (koti).

shlokas.text: विषुवदुदग्दक्षिणतस्तदहोरात्रार्धविष्कम्भः
shlokas.english_draft: North and south of the equator lie the radius circles of diurnal motion (ahoratra-vritta).

shlokas.text: इष्टज्यागुणितमहोरात्रव्यासार्धमेव काष्ठान्त्यम्।वाहोरात्रार्धहृतफलमजाल्लङ्कोदयप्राग्ज्या
shlokas.english_draft: Multiply the desired sine by the radius of the diurnal circle divided by the radius; this yields the right ascension (Lanka rising sine) starting from Aries.

shlokas.text: इष्टापक्रमगुणितामक्षज्यां लम्बकेन हृत्वाया। स्वाहोरात्रे क्षितिजा क्षयवृद्विज्या दिननिशोस्सा
shlokas.english_draft: Multiply the sine of declination by the sine of latitude and divide by the sine of co-latitude; the resulting earth-sine (ksitijya) determines the variation in day and night duration.

shlokas.text: आर्यभटीये८५ स्वाहोरात्रष्टज्यां क्षितिजादवलम्बकाहतांकृत्वा। विष्कम्भाविभक्त दिनस्य गतशेषयोश्शसङकुः
shlokas.english_draft: Multiply the diurnal sine above the horizon by the sine of co-latitude and divide by the radius; the result is the shanku (gnomon/sine of altitude) for the elapsed or remaining daytime.

shlokas.text: परमापक्रमजीवामिष्टज्यार्धाहतो ततीविभजेत् । ज्यालम्बकेन लब्धार्काग्रा पूर्वापरेक्षितिजे
shlokas.english_draft: Multiply the sine of maximum declination by the sine of the desired sun altitude and divide by the co-latitude sine; the quotient is the Sun's amplitude (arka-agra) on the prime vertical horizon.

shlokas.text: सा विषुवज्योंना चैद्विषुवदुदग्लम्बकेन सङ्गुणिता। विषुवज्यया विभक्ता लब्धः पूर्वापरे शकुः
shlokas.english_draft: Subtract the equinoctial sine, multiply by the northern co-latitude sine, and divide by the equinoctial sine; the quotient is the gnomon on the prime vertical.

shlokas.text: क्षितिजादुन्नतभागानां या ज्या सा परोभवेच्छङ कुः। मध्यान्नतभागज्या छाया शोस्तु तस्यैव
shlokas.english_draft: The sine of altitude above the horizon is the gnomon (shankhu); the sine of zenith distance is the shadow of that gnomon.

shlokas.text: मध्यज्योदयजीवासंवगै व्यासदलहृते यत् स्यात् । तन्मध्यज्याकृत्योर्विशेषमूलं स्वदृकक्षेपः
shlokas.english_draft: Multiply the meridian sine by the rising sine and divide by the radius; the square root of the difference between its square and the meridian sine square is the non-division sine (drikkshepa).

shlokas.text: द्रग्द्रकक्षेपकृतिविशेषितस्य मूलं स्वदृग्गतिः कुवशात् ।क्षितिजे स्वादृक्छाया भूव्यासाधू नभोमध्यात्
shlokas.english_draft: The square root of the difference between the squares of parallax-sine and drikkshepa gives the parallax in longitude (drik-gati); parallax varies from zero at zenith to Earth's semi-diameter at the horizon.

shlokas.text: विक्षेपगुणाक्षज्यां लम्बकभक्ता भवेतृणमुदकस्थे। उदये धनमस्तमये दक्षिणगे धनमृणं चन्द्रे
shlokas.english_draft: Multiply latitude sine by celestial latitude and divide by co-latitude sine; the parallax correction is negative or positive depending on northern or southern declination at rising and setting for the Moon.

shlokas.text: विक्षेपापक्रमगुणमुत्क्रमणं विस्तरार्धकृतिभक्तम्। उदगृणधनमुदगयने दक्षिणगे धनमृणं याम्ये
shlokas.english_draft: Multiply declination by latitude andversine, divided by radius square; the deflection correction (valana) is negative or positive during northern and southern solstices.

shlokas.text: चन्द्रो जलमो ऽग्निर्मदभूश्छायापि था तमस्तद्धि।छादयति शशी सूर्य शशिनं महती च भूच्छाया
shlokas.english_draft: The Moon is water, the Sun is fire, the Earth is soil, and its shadow is darkness. The Moon obscures the Sun (solar eclipse), and the great shadow of the Earth obscures the Moon (lunar eclipse).

shlokas.text: स्फुटशशिमासान्ते ऽकं पातासन्नो यंदा प्रविशतीन्दुः ।भूच्छायां पक्षान्ते तदाधिकोनं ग्रहणमध्यम्
shlokas.english_draft: At the end of a synodic month, when the Moon near its node enters the Earth's shadow at full moon (or covers the Sun at new moon), the middle of an eclipse occurs.

shlokas.text: छायाग्रचन्द्रविवरं भूविष्कम्भेण तत् समभ्यस्तम् । भूच्छायया विभक्तं विद्यात्तमसरस्वविष्कम्भम्
shlokas.english_draft: Multiply the distance between the tip of the shadow and the Moon by the Earth's diameter, and divide by the Earth's shadow length; the result is the diameter of the shadow cone at the Moon's distance.

shlokas.text: सम्पर्धिस्य कृतेश्शशिविक्षेपस्य वर्गितं शोध्यम् । स्थित्यर्धमस्य मूलं ज्ञेयं चन्द्रार्कदिनभोगात्
shlokas.english_draft: Subtract the square of the Moon's latitude from the square of the sum of the radii of the obscuring and obscured bodies; the square root converted by the relative motion of Sun and Moon gives half the duration (sthityardha) of the eclipse.

shlokas.text: नस्य वर्गितं यत्तमोमयार्धस्य।विक्षेपकृतिविहीनं तस्मान्मूलं विमर्दार्धम्
shlokas.english_draft: Subtract the square of the latitude from the square of half the difference between the shadow radius and Moon's radius; the square root gives half the duration of total eclipse (vimardardha).

shlokas.text: मध्याहात् क्रमगुणितो ऽक्षो दक्षिणतोऽर्धविस्तरहृतो दिक्स्थित्यर्धाच्चाकैन्दोस्त्रिराशिसहितायनात् स्पर्श
shlokas.english_draft: Calculate the orientation (valana) of the eclipse contact and release from the meridian and horizon using the sine of latitude and declination plus three signs.

shlokas.text: सदसज्ज्ञानसमुद्रात् समुद्भुतं देवताप्रसादेन । सज्ज्ञानोत्तमरत्नं मया निमग्नंस्वमतिनावा
shlokas.english_draft: By the grace of God, I have rescued this jewel of true knowledge from the ocean of true and false knowledge using the boat of my own intellect.

shlokas.text: क्षितिरवियोगाद्दिनकृद्रवीन्दुयोगात्प्रसाधितश्वेन्दुः।शशिताराग्रहयोगात्तथैव ताराग्रहास्सर्वे
shlokas.english_draft: The Sun is established through conjunctions with Earth, the Moon through conjunctions with Sun, and all star-planets through conjunctions with the Moon.

shlokas.text: आर्यभटीयं नान्मा पूर्व स्वायम्भुवं सदा सद्यत् । सुकृतायुषोः प्रणाशं कुरुते प्रतिकञ्चकं योऽस्य
shlokas.english_draft: This work, named Aryabhatiya, reveals the ancient Svayambhuva Siddhanta which is ever true; whoever falsely refutes or distorts it loses the merit of good deeds and longevity.
